review_notes: Read the whole file and the Space.lean simp interface (mk, toProbabilityMeasure, coe_mk, mk_coe, edist_def) plus Mathlib's ProbabilityMeasure.coe_mk. The file has few simp-relevant declarations; it adds no simp lemmas or attributes of its own. I found only one weak interface issue: the measure-level coercion of `mk` has no stated simp lemma, so the file proves it by hand three times. I did not check how simp would behave on these goals, since I can't run Lean. Other uses of simp in the file (`simp [κ]`, `simp only [indicator_apply, hRf]`) looked fine and I saw no competing rules or cycles.

findings.problem: The simp lemma `WassersteinSpace.coe_mk` only states `toProbabilityMeasure (mk μ hμ) = μ`. The measure-level fact `((mk μ hμ : ProbabilityMeasure X) : Measure X) = (μ : Measure X)` has no stated simp form. The file therefore restates it by hand three times (`hmcoe`, `hm₀coe`, `hPcoe`) with the same `congrArg ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure (coe_mk _ _)` term. It then feeds these local equations to `rw`/`simp only`, for example `rw [edist_def, hmcoe, hm₀coe]` and `simp only [edist_def, hPcoe] at h`. This is the boilerplate a canonical simp lemma on the measure coercion would remove. I could not run Lean, so I cannot say whether plain `simp` already closes these goals by chaining `WassersteinSpace.coe_mk` with `ProbabilityMeasure.coe_mk`. The explicit `simp only [edist_def, hPcoe]` suggests the author did not rely on that.
findings.proposed_change: In Space.lean next to `WassersteinSpace.coe_mk`, add a `@[simp]` lemma such as `toMeasure_toProbabilityMeasure_mk (μ : ProbabilityMeasure X) (hμ) : ((toProbabilityMeasure (mk (p := p) μ hμ) : ProbabilityMeasure X) : Measure X) = (μ : Measure X) := rfl`. The name is a placeholder. Then replace `hmcoe`, `hm₀coe` and `hPcoe` with `simp` or `simp [edist_def]` calls. The `mk ⟨κ ∘ₘ P n, _⟩` cases would then go through the existing `ProbabilityMeasure.coe_mk` simp lemma.
findings.benefit: The three duplicated local lemmas and their `congrArg` terms go away. Any later user of `WassersteinSpace.mk` gets the measure-level projection from `simp` without rebuilding it. The `edist_def` rewrites become a single `simp` call.

evidence.excerpt: lemma coe_mk (μ : Measure Ω) (hμ) : toMeasure ⟨μ, hμ⟩ = μ := rfl
